title: Dedicated GPU pool scheduling/autoscale warmup - incident breadcrumbs
content:
Summary:
Short breadcrumbs for the Dedicated GPU pool scheduling/autoscale incident (warmup-related thrash). Notes are a mix of commands I ran, outputs, hypotheses, and next steps. This is an informal timeline/scratchpad - copying here to preserve details before writing the incident postmortem.

Incident TL;DR:
- Time window: 2026-02-19 22:10 - 2026-02-20 02:00 UTC
- Symptoms: repeated scale-up (new GPU nodes) followed by scale-down within ~3-8 minutes, resulting in cold-model latency spikes and request queuing/throttling.
- Impact: brief request errors (5xx) and elevated p95/p99 latency for hosted API customers on dedicated pools.

Timeline / quick hits:
- 22:10: alerts triggered: autoscaler scaling events + p99 latency alert for model x-large (dedicated-pool-a).
- 22:12: verified nodes came up (node provisioning OK), but pods on new nodes reported long image/model load times and Ready=false for ~5-7m.
- 22:18: autoscaler scaled down some nodes thinking they were unused -> evicted warmup progress, returned to scaled own cycle.
- Multiple cycles until we put a temporary min-replicas and increased cooldown (manual mitigation at 23:05).

Commands I ran (most useful outputs pasted inline):

# nodes and labels (confirmed new nodes joined gpu pool)
kubectl get nodes -l gpu-pool=dedicated-pool-a -o wide
# -> several nodes flanked with ProvisionedAt, but STATUS=Ready varied

# autoscaler logs (k8s-cluster-autoscaler / custom nodegroup-autoscaler)
kubectl -n infra logs deploy/cluster-autoscaler --since=1h | egrep "ScaleUp|ScaleDown|unneeded"
2026-02-19T22:11:16 ScaleUp: group=gpu-dedicated-a size:2->4 reason: pending pods (model-serving)
2026-02-19T22:15:43 unneeded: group=gpu-dedicated-a size:4->3 (low usage)
2026-02-19T22:20:01 ScaleUp: group=gpu-dedicated-a size:3->5 reason: pending pods (model-serving)

# describe pod on new node (shows long init/warmup)
kubectl -n inference describe pod model-x-large-abcde
Events:
  Normal  Scheduled  3m  default-scheduler  Successfully assigned inference/model-x-large-abcde to ip-10-0-45-123
  Normal  Pulling    3m  kubelet
  Normal  Pulled     2m  kubelet
  Normal  Created    2m  kubelet
  Normal  Started    2m  kubelet
  Warning Ready     1m  kubelet  Liveness probe failed: HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 503

# container logs show model weight load + KV cache warmup
kubectl -n inference logs model-x-large-abcde -c serve
2026-02-19T22:13:52 INFO loading checkpoint shards (this can take ~90s)
2026-02-19T22:14:40 INFO kv-cache warmup: approx 0/120m tokens populated
2026-02-19T22:17:05 INFO ready_for_traffic=false (latency still > target)

# HPA metrics check
kubectl -n inference get hpa model-x-large-hpa -o yaml
metrics:
  - type: Resource
    resource:
      name: cpu
      target:
        averageUtilization: 60
# HPA is CPU-based, not accounting for warmup latency or custom-ready metric.

Observations / error snippets:
- Autoscaler decided nodes were unneeded shortly after they joined because node-level GPU utilization and cpu were low (model process loading weights, not yet serving).
- Serving process reports 'ready_for_traffic=false' for several minutes while model shards/kv cache load.
- Liveness/readiness probes are simple HTTP checks that return 503 until warmup completes, so K8s considers pods NotReady for a while. Because NotReady pods don't receive traffic but still count toward pending pods? (We need to confirm behaviour with our scheduler).
- HPA is CPU-based; it doesn't capture warmup readiness/queued requests and so doesn't keep pod count stable during warmup window.
- Autoscaler uses short unneeded window (default 5m) and reacts faster than warmup (~7m) -> thrash.

Hypotheses:
1) Warmup time (model weight load + kv cache) > autoscaler unneeded tolerance -> autoscaler scales down before pod finished warming, causing repeated churn.
2) Readiness probe returning 503 keeps pod NotReady; some controllers / load balancer treat NotReady as not serving and autoscaler sees low utilization -> downscale.
3) Node-level autoscaler is oblivious to "warming" metric. It looks at CPU/GPU utilization which will be low during model load.
4) Image/model download/IO contention contributes to slow startup (observed slower pull times on nodes with high disk activity).

Immediate mitigations we tried:
- bumped autoscaler unneeded-time to 12m for gpu-dedicated-a (temp) -> reduced thrash by ~80%.
- set pool min-size to 3 (was 1) during incident window to ensure baseline capacity.
- implemented temporary traffic-slowdown by increasing routing fallback threshold to fallback model variant (reduced load on cold starts).

Longer-term fixes to consider (ranked):
1) Expose a "ready_for_traffic" custom metric and feed it to autoscaler (or use pod annotations so autoscaler doesn't scale down until pods report ready). Could be a custom metric exported to cluster-autoscaler or k8s custom metrics API.
2) Adjust autoscaler unneeded / scale-down-delay for GPU pools by default (e.g., min 10m) or use separate policy for pools known to have long warmup.
3) Add pre-warming step: maintain a small warm pool (min-replicas) with models loaded (cost tradeoff).
4) Improve readiness probe to reflect real readiness (e.g., probe returns 200 when 'ready_for_traffic' is true) and ensure HPA / autoscaler uses that semantics.
5) Pre-pull model artifacts & container images in node init step (daemonset) to reduce image/model load time.
6) Consider marking newly provisioned nodes with a "warming" taint preventing scale-down until nodes have a label/annotation set by the warmup controller.
7) Add a startupProbe config so kubelet treats initial start differently from liveness and avoids killing or marking pods as failed during known-long startup.
8) Instrument and alert on "scale up then down within X minutes" patterns for faster detection.

Open questions / checks to run:
- Does our cluster-autoscaler respect PodDisruptionBudgets or MinReadySeconds? (Check autoscaler code/config).
- Can HPA be configured to use custom metrics that are meaningful for warmup (queued requests, readiness gauge)?
- Are we double-counting pods as pending while NotReady and still influencing scale decisions? Need to verify cluster-autoscaler filters.
- Is there an image/model storage throughput issue on the underlying instance type? Verify node disk I/O metrics during 22:10-22:30.

Next immediate actions (assignments):
- Priya: add a short experiment to flip the readiness probe to depend on ready_for_traffic boolean for model-serving container (staging) and collect warmup durations (target 95th < 5m). (ETA: 2026-03-03)
- Diego: check cluster-autoscaler config + unneeded time for GPU nodegroups, and draft config that sets unneeded-time=12m for gpu-* groups. (ETA: 2026-02-23)
- Samir: run a pre-warm test that brings nodes up and exercises model load with synthetic traffic, measure end-to-end time until ready_for_traffic=true. (ETA: 2026-02-25)
- Me (Ava): create incident write-up + recommended config changes for infra ops (include cost impact analysis for increasing min-size / unneeded-time). (ETA: 2026-03-05)

Notes to include in postmortem draft:
- Root cause: autoscaler scale-down behavior that doesn't account for model warmup time and uses short unneeded window; HPA based on CPU only; readiness semantics not aligned with autoscaler expectations.
- Contributing factors: large model checkpoint sizes leading to long load times; image/model pull bottlenecks; lack of warmup metric.

Scratch - exact autoscaler log snippet to include in postmortem:
"2026-02-19T22:11:16 ScaleUp: group=gpu-dedicated-a size:2->4 reason: pending pods (model-serving)"
"2026-02-19T22:15:43 unneeded: group=gpu-dedicated-a size:4->3 (low usage)"

Potential config proposal (quick):
- For gpu-dedicated-* nodegroups: autoscaler --scale-down-unneeded-time=15m --scale-down-delay-after-add=15m --balance-similar-node-groups=false
- Pool-level: min-size=2, target-size adjustable by traffic tiers, reserve 1 warm replica per active model variant.
- HPA: add custom metric 'requests_ready' or 'ready_pods' to influence scaling.

Final notes / random observations:
- When we bumped unneeded-time to 12m the error rate dropped significantly, but cost increased ~9% for that hour. Need cost-vs-reliability analysis for permanent change.
- Not all models have same warmup time; small models fine, large LLMs (100B+ params) take 3-9m to warm depending on quantization and shards.
- Consider a small "warmup controller" that marks nodes ready after a warmup-healthcheck to keep autoscaler from garbage-collecting them during startup.

If anyone else is digging through logs, grep for "kv-cache warmup" and "ready_for_traffic=false" in inference namespace around 2026-02-19 22:00-23:00.

-- Ava
